evidence.text: Kroger, whose Q2 (May 24-Aug 15, 2026) overlaps most of ACI's Q2 (Jun 21-Sep 12), saw identical sales ex-fuel slow from +1.0% in Q1 to +0.2% in Q2 (IRA drag 130bp then 138bp, so ex-IRA ~2.3% to ~1.6%). It cut its FY identical-sales guide to 0.2-0.8% from 1.0-2.0%, citing 'the macro environment'. Circana data (Grocery Dive, 2026-09-17) show August unit sales of produce -6.7%, bakery -4.3% and meat -2.3% y/y. Applying Kroger's ~60bp two-year-stack slowdown to ACI's Q1 (-0.8% on a +2.8% compare; Q2 compare is +2.2%) gives Q2 identical sales of roughly -0.8% to -1.2%. That is near RBC's -1% and inside ACI's own FY guide of -1.5% to -0.5%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-07-23, Q1 identical sales of -0.8% with a guide cut gave -21.64%. On 2025-10-14, Q2 identical sales of +2.2% with a beat and raise gave +13.63%. Identical sales and the guide move this stock together.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: RBC's -1% and the -1.5% to -0.5% guide already assume a negative comp. What is new is the direction of change: a direct peer slowed in the overlapping weeks, after ACI last spoke on 07-23. If the market had fully priced a weaker-than-Q1 comp, EPS estimates would have drifted down. Instead they 'edged up modestly over 60 days' (Investing.com 2026-10-12), and the stock is +7% over 5 days.
evidence.independence: Circana August unit data via Grocery Dive, a different source: https://www.grocerydive.com/news/august-tough-month-grocery-unit-sales-perishables/830644/ (2026-09-17). Kroger Q1 baseline: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000056873/000110465926075395/tm2618219d1_ex99-1.htm. This is a peer proxy, not an ACI number.

evidence.text: Walmart U.S. (Q2 FY27, reported 2026-08-20) posted mid-single-digit grocery comps 'driven by unit volume gains and share gains' and is putting ~$2.9B of tariff refunds into price rollbacks. ACI's CEO named Walmart, Amazon and Aldi as the main share-takers on the July call. RBC says further downside would come from more ACI 'price investment', which would squeeze the margin the guide depends on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July 2026 cut (-21.6%) was blamed on consumer pressure and share loss to price-led competitors, with investment accelerated 'ahead of expected productivity benefits'. Margin and guide news moves this stock in double digits.
evidence.why_not_priced: The share-loss story has been public since July, and the put skew already pays for downside. The new element is a competitor funding rollbacks with a one-off refund during ACI's Q2 and Q3. If that were priced, the Q2 EBITDA bar would sit at or below RBC's $761M rather than $770M, and EPS estimates would not be rising.
evidence.independence: ACI CEO on July competition: https://www.webull.com/news/15282425096463360. RBC price-investment risk: https://finimize.com/content/rbc-thinks-albertsons-q2-could-miss-by-a-hair. This is a proxy plus inference. ACI has not confirmed new price investment since 07-23.

evidence.text: Kroger kept its FY26 profit guide (adjusted FIFO operating profit $5.0-5.2B, EPS $5.10-5.30) despite cutting sales. Its FIFO gross margin ex-fuel rose 13bp, helped by 'favorable pharmacy mix' and 'strong pharmacy' performance. ACI's Q1 10-Q says pharmacy margins improved 'mainly because of the IRA's impact'. So the same IRA drag that hurts comps (Walmart 125bp, Kroger 138bp, ACI guided ~150bp) supports gross margin, which makes holding the $3.55-3.625B EBITDA guide more plausible than the sales trend alone suggests.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2025-10-14, a guide raise gave +13.63%. On 2026-07-23, a guide cut gave -21.64%. A reaffirmation after a cut has no clean precedent in the seven prints. Kroger's own reaction on 2026-09-11 could not be sourced.
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock trades at ~6.7x the midpoint of its own EPS guide and sits 11.7% above its 52-week low. With 59.5M shares short and the put skew paying for downside, the market is pricing a second cut more than a hold. If a hold were the base case, short interest would not have risen 23% since July and the skew would be flatter. RBC expects the guide to be held.
evidence.independence: Shares one document with the first finding (Kroger 8-K), read for a different line (profit vs sales). ACI's own pharmacy-margin language: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1646972/000164697226000046/aci-20260620.htm. Walmart IRA 125bp: https://www.grocerydive.com/news/walmart-second-quarter-fiscal-2027-earnings-grocery/828292/.

evidence.text: The Q2 bar is set below the pace the FY guide implies. FY guide adjusted EBITDA is $3.55-3.625B less Q1's $1,013M, which leaves $2.54-2.61B for the remaining 36 weeks. FY25 delivered $3,901.5M less Q1's $1,111M less ~$68M for the 53rd week, about $2.72B, so the guide implies -4% to -7% y/y for the rest of the year. Q2 consensus EBITDA of ~$770M is ~-9% and EPS of $0.31-0.33 is -25% to -30% vs $0.44, both worse than that pace and in line with or worse than Q1 (-8.8% EBITDA, -24% EPS). An in-line or slightly better Q2 with a reaffirmed guide would show the guide holding, while a Q2 at consensus forces a back-half acceleration that the market will question.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 EPS of $0.42 missed consensus of $0.54 (-22%) together with a guide cut: -21.64%. Q2 FY25 EPS of $0.44 beat ~$0.39-0.40: +13.63%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Arithmetic from two company releases, against estimates sourced at Earnings Whispers and Investing.com. If the market read Q2 as the trough, sell-side previews would frame a beat as likely. RBC instead previews a small miss ($761M vs $770M), and Earnings Whispers' whisper of $0.34 is the only sign of a lean the other way.
evidence.independence: Q1 FY26 figures and the guide: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1646972/000164697226000041/aciq126earningsrelease.htm. Consensus: https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/ACI. This is my inference across these documents.

evidence.why_not_priced: Each event was public, but none has been read through to the guide. No preview found ties Whitman's arrival to a guide or capital-allocation reset. If it were priced, the event-implied move (6.65%) would sit nearer the last print's 21.6% than the 5.96% median.

evidence.text: At the 2026-09-14 Barclays conference the CFO effectively raised the FY2026 guide. RoTCE is now 'a bit above our 11%', against the 10-11% guided in July. Efficiency is 'a bit better than the 60%' (July: around 60%). NII ex-Markets is 'top end of [5-6%] or a bit better'. He cited 'really good momentum in the third quarter'. H1 RoTCE was about 13%, so a FY a bit above 11% implies H2 at about 9.5-10%. Consensus Q3 EPS of $2.66 against Q2's $3.15 implies a Q3 RoTCE of about 10.5%. The bar therefore sits on the guide, and the print is where the July 'unchanged guide' is formally replaced by the raised one.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 (2026-07-14) Citi beat EPS ($3.15) with the FY guide unchanged and 'muddied' H2 spend messaging. The stock fell 5.29% over the window (-4.4% per Kalkine). Q1 2026 +2.61%, Q4 2025 -3.34%, Q3 2025 +3.89%. This name trades on the guide and the expense outlook, not on the beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It was said publicly four weeks ago, and the stock still fell 1-2% that day with the sector on BofA's warning. What the market has not yet seen is the formal number in the release, or whether the CFO lifts it again given his statement that 'a couple of months have gone by'. If the raise were fully priced, the stock would not be 9.9% below its high with a -3.6% 20-day run-up and puts bid.
evidence.independence: The consensus RoTCE-implied arithmetic draws on several preview sources (Zacks, FMP and Hudson Labs, links in bar). Hudson Labs summarises the same transcript, so it is not independent of the source.

evidence.text: Citi is pulling forward about $500m of its $5bn multi-year investment into H2 2026, 'weighted towards severance' plus card and wealth marketing (Barclays, 2026-09-14). On the Q2 call it said 'in some of the next few quarters, we do expect expense growth to outpace revenue growth'. H1 severance was already about $800m ($500m Q1, $300m Q2). Q2 expenses were $14.2bn. The Q3 expense step-up and its split between Q3 and Q4 are not disclosed. The same H2-spend line sold the Q2 beat.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 traded -5.29% on 'muddied messaging on H2 spend' despite an EPS beat (https://www.fxleaders.com/news/2026/07/15/citigroup-c-stock-price-forecast-citi-slides-as-strong-earnings-fail-to-ease-spending-concerns/).
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely inside the guide. The $500m was quantified on Sept 14, and consensus EPS already steps down from $3.15 to about $2.66. The unpriced part is the timing: if most of the severance lands in Q3, the reported efficiency ratio and EPS could look worse than a model that spreads it evenly. If that were priced, consensus would carry a wide range; TickerLeague shows $2.30-2.73.
evidence.independence: The Barclays transcript (https://www.citigroup.com/rcs/citigpa/storage/public/2026-citigroup-barclays-global-financial-services-conference-transcript.pdf) is a second company document with the $500m figure. It is the same company voice, so not independent.

evidence.text: Peer read since Citi last spoke is soft on the lines Citi leans on. Jefferies' fiscal Q3 (Jun-Aug, reported 2026-09-28) had fixed income revenue -26% YoY and debt underwriting -21%, while advisory (+25%) and ECM (+69%) were records. Goldman's CEO said on 2026-09-16 that FICC would be 'slightly softer' and IB 'much more muted'. BofA guided Q3 IB fees down 10-20% YoY with trading flat. Citi's Markets is FICC-heavy and its IB leans to DCM, but Citi guided Markets +MSD and IB +LSD on 2026-09-14 with about 2.5 months of the quarter known.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Markets drove the Q1 and Q2 2026 beats (Q2 Markets +17%). The July call warned that the H1-to-H2 Markets decline (historically about 20%) 'could be greater this year'. No resolved print to cite where Markets alone missed.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The sector sold off 2026-09-15 on BofA (C -1-2%), and the Jefferies print came after Citi spoke but covers Jun-Aug only. Citi's own later guide on the same quarter is the more direct series, so this proxy is sized below it. If it were unpriced, C would not already have underperformed 20d (-3.6%).
evidence.independence: Goldman CFO/CEO remarks: https://kfgo.com/2026/09/16/goldman-ceo-says-fixed-income-currencies-commodities-business-slightly-softer-in-q3/. BofA warning: https://parameter.io/bank-of-america-bac-slides-5-on-investment-banking-revenue-warning-for-q3/. Three separate counterparties.

evidence.text: The Citibank Credit Card Issuance Trust 10-D for the due period ending 2026-08-26 shows 30+ day delinquency of about 1.29%. That is down from 1.32% in July and from 1.42% a year earlier. The credit-loss component is 2.03% (July 1.90%, June 2.25%). Card credit looks benign into Q3, consistent with U.S. card NCL toward the low end of the 4-4.5% FY guide and room for reserve stability or release.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit has not been the line Citi traded on in the last four prints. Moves were explained by guide and expense messaging.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The CFO said credit is stable and delinquencies are down YoY on 2026-09-14. The trust is a small (~$19bn), seasoned slice of the card book, so it is a proxy for the reported NCL rather than the number itself.
evidence.independence: July 10-D (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001108348/000119312526353756/d138267dex99.htm) and Barclays transcript credit remarks.

evidence.text: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, its first hike since 2023, with a hawkish dot plot. Citi's NII ex-Markets is volume-driven and asset-sensitive, so this supports the 'top end or better' NII guide and a firmer Q4/2027 NII outlook. It is a headwind to AOCI, TBV and CET1 (12.8% vs a 12.6% target). The rate decision source is secondhand.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific to Citi in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: Macro, public and transmitted through models already. The only unpriced part is whether management quantifies an NII upgrade on the call. If it were fully priced, Visible Alpha's +11% Q3 NII estimate would already include it; the 2026-10-10 Visible Alpha preview shows NIM declining.
evidence.independence: Proxy. The CFO said on 2026-09-14 that 'rates around the world [have] an upward bias' (Barclays transcript), but did not quantify it.

evidence.text: JPMorgan and Wells Fargo (about 7:00 ET) and Goldman Sachs (7:30 ET) all report on 2026-10-13 before Citi's 8:00 ET release, so the sector's read of trading and IB will be set before Citi's numbers land, inside the same window. BofA and Morgan Stanley report the following morning, outside the window.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-07-14 the same cluster reported the same morning and Citi fell 5.29%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sign cannot be known before the release. It is filed so that judges know a large part of the window's move is sector beta set by three peers' prints.
evidence.independence: Calendar also in the sweep row and Citi's own release (https://www.citigroup.com/global/news/press-release/2026/citi-third-quarter-2026-earnings-call).

evidence.text: Capital return. evidence.why_not_priced: An inference from wording. A Q3 buyback of about $4bn (the Q2 pace) is plausibly what models carry. If a slowdown were expected, previews would flag it, and none found does.
evidence.independence: Shares the Barclays transcript with finding 1. Q2 call: $4bn bought back in Q2, CET1 target about 12.6% (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/21/citi-c-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).

evidence.text: The US comp bar of +1.1% requires a two-year stack acceleration. Q2 2026 US comps were +0.1% on a +3.4% lap (two-year stack +3.5). Q3 laps +5.2% (Q3 2025, the Best Deal Ever plus Parmesan Stuffed Crust quarter), so holding the Q2 two-year stack implies about -1.7%. The Q3 product innovation (the Detroit-style 'Domino') launched only on 2026-08-31, about one week before the 12-week fiscal Q3 closed (~2026-09-06, since Q2 ended 2026-06-14). Q3's main lever was re-running the same $9.99 Best Deal Ever with Stuffed Crust added (2026-06-15 to 07-26), against last year's version of that same deal. Offset: the CFO said on the Q2 call that the ticket drag would be 'much more modest' in Q3, and order counts grew 'meaningfully' in Q2.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: US comps are the line this stock trades on. Q1 2026: +0.9% vs ~2.5% expected plus a guide cut, -8.84%. Q2 2026: +0.1% vs ~0.6% expected, but order counts grew, +2.11% (about +7% premarket). Q4 2025: comps beat, +4.1%. Q3 2025: +5.2% beat, +3.91%. A comp miss without a guide cut has not been punished.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Zacks consensus still sits at +1.1%, which assumes the two-year stack improves by ~2.8 points. If the market had priced the lap, the comp bar would be near zero or negative. Partly priced: the +7.1 put skew and a run of target cuts already lean this way.
evidence.independence: Q3 2025 comp of +5.2% from the company's own Q3 2025 release (https://ir.dominos.com/node/24041, 2025-10-14). Launch date of the Domino from NRN (https://nrn.com/quick-service/domino-s-new-pizza-targets-solo-diners). Promo dates from the company release (https://dominos.gcs-web.com/node/24646, 2026-06-15). evidence.text: Neither FY26 guide line has room left after Q3. US comps are +0.5% year to date against a 'low single digits' FY guide. International comps are -0.2% year to date against a low-single-digit guide that already includes a World Cup benefit. FY26 operating income growth is guided at mid-to-high single digits ex-FX, against Q2 operating income of only +2.6% ex-FX. The US store-growth guide was already trimmed in July to about 175. This is Joe Jordan's first call as CEO (effective 2026-10-01); he was COO and US president, so he is an internal successor. The CFO said 2027 detail comes with Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The April 2026 cut of the US comp guide (from ~3% to low single digits) plus a comp miss gave -8.84%, the largest reaction in the history. In July the guide was reaffirmed apart from a trim to US units, and the stock rose 2.11%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Seven price-target cuts between 2026-09-23 and 2026-10-09 (Guggenheim 440 to 325, JPM 380 to 350, Redburn 270 to 260, Baird 350 to 325, RBC 350 to 325, Gordon Haskett 370 to 340, Morgan Stanley 370 to 357) suggest the Street models the bottom of the ranges. A formal cut of the international or operating-income guide would still be a new statement; if fully priced, the skew would be flatter after the drop.
evidence.independence: YTD comp figures come from the Q2 release (https://www.franchising.com/news/20260720_dominos_pizza_announces_second_quarter_2026_financial_results.html), which shares its numbers with the first finding. evidence.text: International read-throughs from master franchisees for the overlapping period are mixed but better than Q2, against an easier lap. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: International rarely drives this stock; in Q1 2026 international comps of -0.4% came with US weakness, and the reaction is attributed to US comps and guidance. International franchise royalties are estimated at $78.5M of $1.17B in revenue.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Jubilant figure is five days old and sits on an Indian exchange that US restaurant analysts do not quote. evidence.text: The 10-Q cover shows 49,978,138 shares outstanding at 2026-07-31. Q2 average diluted shares were about 51.9M ($58.6M GAAP NI / $1.13 diluted EPS), after 1.55M shares (3.01%) were bought back in Q2. Flat Q2 adjusted earnings of $58.9M on about 50.1M Q3 diluted shares gives about $1.18. With NII growth on Q2's 11.6% annualised loan growth, a provision back below Q2's $10.1M, or both, the $1.21 consensus is reachable to modestly beatable.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EPS of $1.14 against $1.15 (a slight miss) and a revenue miss still traded +3.23% over the session window. Q3 2025, a $1.07 adjusted beat against $1.03, traded +4.07%. The EPS line has been rewarded mildly or forgiven.
evidence.why_not_priced: Sell-side models will include the buyback, so this is mostly priced. What may not be priced is the provision normalising after Q2's $10.1M spike, which was taken on three NPL relationships. If the market fully expected a clean beat, the stock would not sit 5% above its 52-week low with shorts up 40% in the last fortnight of September.
evidence.independence: Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000052/a2q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm) for the buyback, Q2 provision and NI. It is a different document from the 10-Q cover but the same company data, so read it as one company-level arithmetic, not two independent sources.

evidence.text: The Q2 NIM guide (FY ex-accretion 3.70-3.80%) explicitly assumed one Fed hike in Q3 2026. The FOMC did hike 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, 12-0. FBK says it is slightly asset sensitive and that a hike helps 'to the tune of a couple million dollars'. The rate path therefore matched the guide's assumption, so the margin guide is unlikely to be cut on rates, but the Q3 benefit is only about two weeks.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: NIM has been stable to rising (3.68% in Q2 2025, 3.94% in Q1 2026, 3.95% in Q2 2026). I found no clean record of the stock reacting to a NIM surprise in isolation.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the hike is public and inside the company's own guide. It matters only because a guide cut on rates is less likely. If the market feared margin pressure, regional-bank peers would have sold off on the hike, and I found no evidence that they did.
evidence.independence: Q2 call transcript, rate assumption and asset-sensitivity quotes (https://www.webull.com/news/15226549103125504), a different document from the Fed release.

evidence.text: On 2026-09-24 FBK issued $125M of 6.625% fixed-to-floating subordinated notes due 2036, 'to support [FirstBank's] growth'. The prospectus says FirstBank's dividend capacity to the parent under Tennessee law 'has been substantially utilized'. That follows Q2 buybacks of 3.01% of shares and CET1 falling to 11.0% from 11.5%. Rule 4 question, what does the money buy: growth capital, corroborated by Q2 loans HFI +11.6% annualised, above the mid-to-high-single-digit guide. It also signals that holdco buyback capacity is constrained and adds about $2M a quarter of interest from Q4.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print followed a debt raise in the record I could see.
evidence.why_not_priced: The raise is public, but the call will show whether the Q3 buyback pace and loan growth continue. If the market had read the raise as a growth signal, the stock would not have drifted from about $58 to $53 since late August. If it had read it as distress, I would expect a sharper drop and wider credit spreads, and I found neither.
evidence.independence: 8-K of 2026-09-24 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000121390026103052/ea0306481-8k_fbfinancial.htm), the same transaction. Loan growth from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000052/a2q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm) corroborates the growth use.

evidence.text: Credit is the swing line. Q2 NPAs rose to 1.14% of assets from 0.98% on three relationships: two individually evaluated CRE credits with about $3.5M of specific reserves, and one 'well-collateralized credit with a near-term workout plan'. The Sept 17 investor deck shows the CECL macro inputs as 'modestly softer' (Moody's national unemployment 4.5% in 3Q26 and 4.8% in 4Q26, house price index -1.5% and -2.9%). Further migration or a reserve build would keep Q3 provision at or above Q2's $10.1M. A successful workout would let NPAs fall.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print with rising NPAs and a provision jump to $10.1M from $3.0M still closed the session window +3.23%. Credit has not been punished on this name so far.
evidence.why_not_priced: The direction of the workout is unknowable before the release, and the deck's macro inputs are Q2-dated. If the market expected a clean resolution, short interest would not be at a one-year high. If it expected a large loss, the stock would be below its 52-week low.
evidence.independence: Q2 call commentary on the three credits (https://www.webull.com/news/15226549103125504) and the Q2 release. These are company documents, not an independent credit series. I searched Tennessee courts for borrower litigation and found nothing.

evidence.text: FINRA short interest rose 40.5% to 3.0M shares (about 6.1% of shares outstanding, 3.8 days to cover) at the 2026-09-30 settlement. That is the fourth consecutive increase and a one-year high, into a stock 5% above its 52-week low. A clean print would push shorts to cover, a supporting flow. A credit surprise would validate them.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reactions alternate in sign: +3.23, -2.30, -1.41, +4.07, -4.57, -1.97, +2.21. Median absolute 2.3%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Short interest is published but seldom priced into a regional bank's day-of reaction. At 6% and 3.8 days it is not crowded, so this is a small asymmetry, not a squeeze setup.
evidence.independence: Stock about $58 in late August against $53.48 now (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/FBK) and the sealed baseline tape: -13.85% from the 52-week high. Same direction, different source.

evidence.text: Mortgage rates rose in early Q3: the MBA put the 30-year fixed at 6.65% in the week ending July 10, the highest since August 2025. evidence.why_not_priced: Small and likely already in models. It is a proxy for a minor segment. The rest of the company (NII, about 85% of revenue) would have to soften too for this to matter.
evidence.independence: This is a proxy; the company has not confirmed Q3 mortgage volumes. For an asset-sensitive balance sheet that supports holding or nudging up the FY NII guide and a higher Q4 exit rate. If it were fully priced, the stock would not sit 18% below the post-Q2 high on flat estimates. The residual is the size of the FY raise and of the MCR beat beyond 90.1%, which the CFO did not quantify.

evidence.text: On the Q2 call the company guided a 'two-thirds, one-third first half to back half mix' with 'slightly more earnings in 3Q relative to 4Q'. On H1 adjusted EPS of $13.61 and an FY guide of $19.50-20.00, that implies Q3 of about $3.0-3.4. The $4.12 consensus therefore already requires Q3 to beat the company's own cadence by ~$0.7-1.1 (20-35%). A Q3 that beats the guide's cadence but lands below $4.12 would headline as a miss.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two quarters beat consensus by ~10% (Q1, $7.23 vs ~$6.6) and ~30% (Q2, $6.38 vs ~$4.9) while the guide sat far below. Management has consistently printed above both cadence and street this year, so this bar risk has not materialised in 2026.
evidence.why_not_priced: Previews quote $4.12 against last year's $2.92 and do not reconcile it with the company's H2 cadence. If the market were anchoring on the guide-implied ~$3.2, consensus would sit near that, as Zacks' $3.66 in July roughly did. The $4.12 bar means the street expects a beat versus the guide, so the risk is that the beat is smaller than the street has built in.

evidence.text: The Q3 call is the first likely look at 2027. On ~$94B of Optum Health revenue, +2pts is about +$1.9B pre-tax, or ~+$1.6/share. Together with Medicaid that supports the $22.44 FY27 consensus (+13%), even though commercial recovery is pushed beyond 2027 and 2026 carries $860M of PPD and a light flu season.

If the market believed $22.44, the multiple would not sit at what TIKR calls a trough of ~18x forward. The discount looks like doubt about 2027 (2.48% MA final rate, 15% stars decline, sticky commercial trend), which a confirming 2027 view would address. The size of the 2027 view is inference from company targets, not a disclosed number.
evidence.independence: Hudson Labs preview (2026-09-28) lists the same 2027 segment targets from company statements (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/unitedhealth-q3-2026-earnings-preview-unh-guidance-margins), so it is not independent.
